rulings.challenge_claim: One challenge holds that the rejected-alternative sentence assigns the boundary it sets aside to a tier-3 mark layer when the grouping in question is a tier-1 letter stanza, and that three of the span's four translation citations reproduce an open multi-verse quotation as if each verse closed its own. The converging challenge raises the same tier mislabel, adds that the two closing verses are said to carry plural object suffixes when their plural elements are prepositional and nominal, and flags a positional reference to a neighbouring unit.
rulings.grounds: Same defect from both sides on the tier point, and it stands: 3:46, 3:47 and 3:48 all carry the pe letter at position 16 of this chapter's pinned pe-before-ayin order, so the grouping the rejected alternative sets aside is a tier-1 letter stanza. The mark layer is a separate tier-3 single-witness layer that in this chapter falls only at stanza ends (sweep: 22 marked verses of 66 - 3:3, 3:6 ... 3:66), so the mark at 3:48 corroborates the stanza rather than constituting it; the field as written weighs a tier-1 person shift against 'the triplet's own tier-3 parashah-mark symmetry', downgrading a tier-1 counterweight. The suffix finding stands too: the plural elements of 3:46 are עָלֵ֛ינוּ (preposition plus first-plural) and אֹיְבֵֽינוּ (noun plus first-plural), and of 3:47 לָ֖נוּ (preposition plus first-plural), all byte tier; the section's plural verbal object suffixes stand at וַֽתִּרְדְּפֵ֔נוּ (oshb:Lam.3.43, byte tier) and תְּשִׂימֵ֖נוּ (oshb:Lam.3.45, byte tier), outside both verses, and the definite 'the plural object suffixes' names a class the row never introduced. The positional-reference finding stands: a verse is held 'for the following span' rather than named by its verse. The translation-quote half is REFUTED on bytes: all four quoted lines are verbatim substrings of the verses they cite (3:40, 3:42, 3:46, 3:47), so no fidelity mismatch exists - the enclosing curly pair is the sanctioned delimiter for verbatim translation English, not a reproduction of the witness's own marks. The byte picture behind that half is also inexact: the witness carries opening marks at 3:42, 3:43 and 3:46 and a single closing mark at 3:47, so the run is not one continuous open quotation; and translation punctuation is tier-4 never-evidence, so those marks could not carry weight in either direction. The seam itself is sound and no respan is proposed: the mid-stanza cut is licensed by a disclosed tier-1 person shift that is byte-true, first-plural לָ֖נוּ at 3:47 turning to first-singular עֵינִ֔י (oshb:Lam.3.48, byte tier), and the mark disclosures at 3:39, 3:42 and 3:45 are correct and correctly classed.
rulings.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: replace 'the triplet's own tier-3 parashah-mark symmetry' with the tier-1 letter-stanza description (the pe stanza covering 3:46-3:48) and keep the mark at 3:48 as separate tier-3 single-witness corroboration. boundary_rationale: replace 'both still carrying the plural object suffixes' with the byte-accurate class - first-plural prepositional and nominal suffixes at 3:46-3:47 - and, if a verbal-object-suffix claim is wanted, anchor it at 3:43 and 3:45. device_notes: replace 'held for the following span' with a verse-anchored formulation naming 3:48. Tests the cure must pass: every tier label re-derived against the acrostic letter data (pe at 3:46-3:48) and the mark inventory (marks in this chapter only at 3:3 ... 3:66); the residual-register arm returning no positional neighbouring-unit reference; the suffix class re-read from the pointed bytes of 3:46-3:47. No work order attaches to the refuted quotation half. Cross-row candidate: the same tier mislabel stands on both sides of this seam.

rulings.challenge_claim: Both challenges hold that the cross-seam disclosure labels the pe stanza the span leaves behind a tier-3 signal, demoting a tier-1 letter stanza; one adds register residuals - a positional reference to a neighbouring unit and a rejected-alternative ground that is a cross-unit reference rather than a verse-anchored one.
rulings.grounds: Byte-verified and convergent. The letters run pe at 3:46, 3:47 and 3:48 (position 16), ayin at 3:49-3:51 (17) and tsade at 3:52-3:54 (18) in this chapter's pinned pe-before-ayin order; the grouping disclosed 'as a tier-3 signal' is therefore the tier-1 letter stanza itself. The tier-3 single-witness layer is the mark, and in this chapter marks fall only at stanza ends (sweep: 22 marked verses of 66; inside this span 3:48, 3:51 and 3:54, each disclosed and correctly named samekh, with no mark claimed at any unmarked verse). Weighed from both sides, the one seam is argued against a downgraded counterweight in both directions, so the disclosed mid-stanza exception rests on a tier assignment the bytes do not support even though the exception itself is warranted: the opening ground is byte-true, first-singular עֵינִ֔י (oshb:Lam.3.48, byte tier) resuming after the plural section that closes with לָ֖נוּ (oshb:Lam.3.47, byte tier). The register residuals stand: 'argued in the previous span' is a positional reference to a neighbouring unit, and 'the reason offered against it on the other side of the same seam' is a cross-unit reference carrying no verse anchor. The span, its letters and its mark disclosures are otherwise correct, and no ketiv/qere note falls inside 3:48-3:54.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace 'that grouping is disclosed here as a tier-3 signal' with the tier-1 letter-stanza statement (the pe stanza covering 3:46-3:48) and carry the mark at 3:48 separately as tier-3 single-witness corroboration; replace 'argued in the previous span' with the verse range 3:46-3:47. strongest_rejected_alternative: restate the ground in verse-anchored terms - the first-plural to first-singular person shift across 3:47 and 3:48 - instead of 'the reason offered against it on the other side of the same seam'. Tests the cure must pass: tier labels re-derived against the letter data and the mark inventory; the residual-register arm returning no positional or non-verse-anchored cross-unit reference; the mid-stanza exception still naming a disclosed tier-1 reason on both sides of the seam.

rulings.challenge_claim: The closing verbs are labeled imperatives, but 3:64-3:66 are second-masculine-singular prefix-conjugation forms and the span's one true imperative stands at 3:63, inverting the disclosed discourse ground.
rulings.grounds: Byte-verified. תָּשִׁ֨יב (oshb:Lam.3.64, byte tier), תִּתֵּ֤ן (oshb:Lam.3.65, byte tier) and תִּרְדֹּ֤ף (oshb:Lam.3.66, byte tier) each open their verse with the tav conjugation prefix - which is precisely what places all three on the tav line at letter position 22 - and are second-masculine-singular prefix-conjugation forms, not imperatives. The span's one imperative is הַבִּ֔יטָה (oshb:Lam.3.63, byte tier), standing inside the verses the rationale assigns to petition-report; under the single-letter prefix-tolerance test with finals-normalized needles that form stands in 4 verses book-wide (1:11, 2:20, 3:63, 5:1). The two translation lines the row itself quotes render the verbs as futures at 3:64 and 3:66, so neither witness supports the label. Form-class labels are byte-checkable claims and the staged extract carries no morphology layer, so each must be argued from the pointed form; here the disclosed discourse ground - a shift from petition-report to imperative imprecation beginning at 3:64 - is inverted at the form level, and the same ground carries the rejected alternative, so the unit's sole discourse warrant fails. The rest of the span checks: shin and tav stanzas at positions 21 and 22 close the alphabet at the poem seam, the three forms are verse-initial as claimed (sweep: 3 verses), the chapter's single PE mark falls at 3:66 (sweep: 1 of 66 verses) and is kept distinct from the samekh at 3:63 and the preceding 3:60, and every Hebrew run and translation line collates. A confidence of high with no frontier flag is not supportable while the stated discourse ground is a form-class error.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace 'a threefold imperative-future imprecation' and 'shift from petition-report to imperative imprecation' with the byte-accurate form class - three verse-initial second-masculine-singular prefix-conjugation forms - and restate the discourse change as a turn from report of what has been heard to prospective retribution; if an imperative is to be named in this span, anchor it to הַבִּ֔יטָה at 3:63 and redraw which verses count as petition-report. strongest_rejected_alternative: restate its ground on the corrected form class. confidence: lower from high, and set frontier_flag_considered true unless a re-derived tier-1 ground carries the close. Tests the cure must pass: every form-class label in the row re-derived from the pointed bytes (imperative versus prefix-conjugation at 3:63 through 3:66); the corrected ground must still license a two-stanza unit ending on the poem seam; and the confidence must match the surviving warrant.

rulings.challenge_claim: Both challenges hold that the span splices Hebrew from 4:3 and quotes its translation line with no ketiv/qere disclosure anywhere in the row, so the two declared false positives should be refuted rather than confirmed; one adds that the plural jackal reading silently adopts one of the two competing readings.
rulings.grounds: Byte-verified and convergent - one defect, two framings. 4:3 is one of the book's two doubled-note ketiv/qere verses (inventory: 22 notes over 20 verses, 2 notes at 4:3), and both pairs stand in the source line: unpointed ketiv תנין against pointed qere תַּנִּים֙, and unpointed ketiv כי ענים against pointed qere כַּיְעֵנִ֖ים (oshb:Lam.4.3; ketiv forms byte-exact as consonantal skeletons, qere forms at byte tier). device_notes splices בַּת עַמִּ֣י from that same verse at byte tier and boundary_rationale quotes its translation line, verbatim on my own check; no field of the row carries any ketiv/qere disclosure. The disclosure requirement carries no materiality exception, so both declared false positives are refuted and stand as confirmed defects. The added point holds as well: the rationale's nursing jackals is plural, which is the qere, against a singular ketiv - one of two competing readings presented as the text at the very verse where the row also anchors its recurrence claim. The remainder of the row checks: the opening cry is verse-initial at 4:1 (sweep: 4 verses book-wide, verse-initial in 3, the non-initial site being 4:2); the two-token daughter-of-my-people phrase stands in 5 verses book-wide (2:11, 3:48, 4:3, 4:6, 4:10), matching the cited digit; letters aleph through vav are positions 1-6 of this chapter's pe-before-ayin order and are correctly not called the standard one; every verse of the span carries a mark, each disclosed as single-witness, with the preceding PE at 3:66 named and never conflated with samekh; and all three quoted translation lines are verbatim.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: add a ketiv/qere disclosure for 4:3 naming both notes as single-witness apparatus and stating which of the two readings the jackals wording follows, or restate the wording so that it chooses neither. boundary_rationale: keep the quoted translation line and carry the same disclosure in-field, so that the splice and the quote each sit beside it. Tests the cure must pass: with the splice and the translation quote retained, the prose-dual and quote-coverage disclosure warnings that raised the original two flags must return zero; and the two queue entries must be re-dispositioned from declared false positive to confirmed and repaired.

rulings.challenge_claim: A translation quote sits unpaired beyond its field's ref window, the named-once claim carries no digit-bearing sweep, and the two-token phrase that straddles the front seam is described as not crossing it.
rulings.grounds: All three findings verified. First, the field's opening quoted line is verbatim at 4:7 on my own check, but the only translation ref anywhere near it points to 4:11 and stands 318 characters past the quote's end, so the nearest ref names a different verse than the quote; the quote-plus-inline-ref convention is unmet in substance even though a ref does stand somewhere in the field. Second, device_notes states the divine name is named once in this group with no adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming its object and unit. The fact is byte-true - the name stands in 1 of the span's 5 verses, at יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Lam.4.11, byte tier), in 3 verses of this chapter (4:11, 4:16, 4:20) and 32 book-wide, with no Adonai title anywhere in this chapter - but an exclusivity claim must carry the digit and the named object beside it and is never tier-dampened. Third, the two-token daughter-of-my-people phrase stands at 4:6, the verse immediately behind this span's front seam, and again at 4:10 inside it (sweep: 5 verses book-wide), so a device true at the bytes sits on both sides of the row's own seam; saying it frames rather than crosses this boundary denies the straddle that both-sides weighing requires. The subsidiary point that the parenthesis omits a third site at 4:3 does not stand as a separate defect: that parenthesis makes no book-wide census claim, and the site outside the seam is carried at its full five-verse sweep in the adjacent argument. Otherwise sound: the verse-initial form at 4:7, letters zayin through kaf at positions 7-11, every span verse marked and disclosed with the preceding 4:6 named, the second quoted line verbatim at 4:11, and no ketiv/qere note inside 4:7-4:11.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: place an inline web ref for 4:7 immediately beside the first quoted translation line. device_notes: replace 'YHWH is named once in this group' with an object-and-unit sweep citation - the divine name stands in 1 of this group's 5 verses, at 4:11 (sweep: 3 verses in this chapter, 32 verses book-wide) - and replace 'frames rather than crosses this span's own boundary' with an explicit straddle disclosure weighing the 4:6/4:7 seam from both sides. Tests the cure must pass: the quote-pairing arm must bind every quoted translation line to a ref naming that same verse inside its proximity window; the exclusivity arm must find a digit-bearing sweep adjacent to the named-once claim; and the cross-seam cohesion sentence must name the device on both sides of the seam.

rulings.challenge_claim: One challenge holds that the rejected alternative names content not found in the cited earlier verses; the converging challenge calls that same alternative unrealizable as a contiguous span, and adds that the front seam rests on topic alone with no person shift disclosed and that the divine-name note misplaces the 4:11 site.
rulings.grounds: The two rejected-alternative findings are one defect in two framings, and it holds. The nobles term stands only at 4:7, נְזִירֶ֨יהָ֙ (oshb:Lam.4.7, byte tier; sweep: 1 verse book-wide), outside this span; 4:12-4:14 carry the disbelieving kings of the earth, the sins of prophets and priests, and blood-polluted wanderers, with no nobles and no elders falling; the only elders term in the wider group is the qere וּזְקֵנִ֖ים (oshb:Lam.4.16, byte tier), later than 4:15 rather than earlier. An alternative that ends the group at 4:14 while keeping 4:15 with the nobles therefore describes no contiguous span the witness carries, and its content cannot be checked against the witnessed verses. The divine-name note fails on bytes: the name stands at 4:11, 4:16 and 4:20 in this poem (sweep: 3 verses in the chapter, 32 book-wide), and 4:11 is the verse immediately before this span's onset, so under an exact tiling it closes the preceding unit and cannot have opened it; the same sentence also refers to a neighbouring unit positionally rather than by verse. The front-seam finding holds with one refinement. There is no voice or addressee change across 4:11 and 4:12 - no first-plural element stands anywhere in 4:1-4:16 (sweep: 0 verses; the two plural-ending tokens there, הֶאֱמִ֨ינוּ֙ (oshb:Lam.4.12, byte tier) and חָנָֽנוּ (oshb:Lam.4.16, byte tier), are third-plural perfects) - and neither corroborating layer can discriminate a seam inside this poem, since every verse opens a new acrostic letter and every verse carries a mark (sweep: 21 samekh and 1 pe over the poem's 22 verses). The refinement: the bytes do offer an undisclosed tier-1 ground the field could have argued, since 4:12 introduces new grammatical participants, מַלְכֵי אֶ֔רֶץ and יֹשְׁבֵ֣י תֵבֵ֑ל (oshb:Lam.4.12, byte tier), where the preceding verses run on the city and her people. The corrected finding is that the seam's tier-1 warrant is undisclosed and the confidence unhedged, not that no warrant exists. The ketiv/qere disclosure in the row is accurate: notes stand at 4:12 and 4:16 and nowhere else in the span, both unspliced.
rulings.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the unrealizable alternative with one naming a contiguous verse range the witness carries (for example a group closing at 4:13 weighed against one closing at 4:16), and either drop the nobles reference or anchor it to 4:7. device_notes: correct 'the mention at 4:11 that opened the group before it' to state that the site stands at 4:11, the verse immediately before this span, and re-anchor the sentence to verses rather than to a neighbouring unit. boundary_rationale: disclose the seam ground explicitly - either name the participant introduction at 4:12 as the tier-1 signal, or state that the seam is thematic, set frontier_flag_considered true and lower confidence accordingly. Tests the cure must pass: every rejected alternative must resolve to a contiguous verse range the witness carries; every divine-name statement must be re-derived against the chapter census 4:11, 4:16 and 4:20; the seam ground must name a signal class rather than a topic; and the residual-register arm must return no positional neighbouring-unit reference.

rulings.challenge_claim: The seam taken is the byte-correct one but the case made for it is not: the tested alternative is called the more probable seam on a ground that refutes it, the first-plural onset claim ships without its digit, and the closing verse is retitled past its own bytes.
rulings.grounds: All three findings verified. First, the onset claim is byte-true and undigited: no first-plural element stands anywhere in 4:1-4:16 (sweep: 0 verses; the two plural-ending tokens there are third-plural perfects), while 4:17-4:20 carry fifteen first-plural tokens over four consecutive verses (5, 5, 3 and 2 respectively). boundary_rationale asserts that the plural enters at the ayin line - an onset claim of the class that must carry an adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming object and unit - and carries none, which leaves the row's strongest evidence as its only uncounted claim. One refinement on the challenge's own count-object: the census mixes pronominal suffixes with first-plural verbal afformatives, צִפִּ֔ינוּ (oshb:Lam.4.17, byte tier) and אָמַ֔רְנוּ (oshb:Lam.4.20, byte tier), so the object is properly named as first-plural elements rather than suffixes; the digits and the zero result are unaffected. Second, the tested alternative is self-refuting and internally incoherent: the field names 4:16 as the more probable seam while the row takes 4:17, and grounds that preference on 4:16's verbs staying third person about them rather than us - which is the strongest argument for the seam actually taken. The only plural-looking form at 4:16 is חָנָֽנוּ (oshb:Lam.4.16, byte tier), a third-plural perfect. Third, the gloss exceeds its splice: the field calls 4:20 the king's capture, but the spliced phrase is מְשִׁ֣יחַ יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Lam.4.20, byte tier), the book's only anointed term (sweep: 1 verse book-wide), and the row's own translation quote renders it the anointed of Yahweh; the one king term in this poem, מַלְכֵי אֶ֔רֶץ (oshb:Lam.4.12, byte tier), denotes the nations' kings. The ketiv/qere handling is sound: the pair עודינה against qere עוֹדֵ֨ינוּ֙ at 4:17 is spliced with both forms and disclosed in-field, and the inventory carries no other note and no paseq inside the span; the letters at positions 17-20 and the mark disclosures from 4:16 through 4:20 are correct.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: attach a digit-bearing sweep to the plural-onset claim naming its object and unit (first-plural elements: 0 verses across 4:1-4:16; 15 tokens over the four verses 4:17-4:20), and replace 'the king's capture' with a gloss no wider than the splice. strongest_rejected_alternative: restate the alternative so that its stated ground would favour the alternative rather than the seam actually taken, and remove 'the more probable seam' unless the seam itself is moved. Tests the cure must pass: the exclusivity and onset arm must find an adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming object and unit; every rejected alternative must be argued on a ground that would favour it; and gloss extent must not exceed splice extent when the sentence is read back whole.

rulings.challenge_claim: The span, its address evidence and its flagged concern all hold, but the cohesion ground given for keeping the two verses together names shared vocabulary that stands in one verse apiece, the genre label ascribes a speech class the book nowhere carries, and a substrate-signal key names the poem-closing mark.
rulings.grounds: The cohesion finding stands: the cup term כּ֔וֹס (oshb:Lam.4.21, byte tier) stands in 4:21 only (sweep: 1 verse book-wide) and 4:21 carries no iniquity term at all, while עֲוֺנֵךְ֙ (oshb:Lam.4.22, byte tier) stands twice in 4:22 and nowhere in 4:21 - so the shared cup and iniquity vocabulary offered as the reason for one span does not exist. What is genuinely shared is the two-token address to Edom, בַּת אֱד֔וֹם (oshb:Lam.4.21, byte tier), standing in both verses (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, both inside this span), which the row's device note already names. The refinement is on the challenge's own census: its figure of 4 verses for the iniquity term matches neither reading of its object - the suffixed token stands in 2 verses (2:14, 4:22), and the lexeme, swept with a finals-normalized needle, stands in 5 (2:14, 4:6, 4:13, 4:22, 5:7); the four-verse figure drops עֲוֺ֣ן (oshb:Lam.4.6, byte tier) because a medial-nun needle does not match the final nun there. The genre finding stands: 4:21 runs on second-feminine-singular imperatives שִׂ֤ישִׂי וְשִׂמְחִי֙ (oshb:Lam.4.21, byte tier) and second-feminine-singular prefix forms, and 4:22 on third-masculine-singular verbs with second-feminine-singular suffixes; no first-person divine speech and no messenger formula stands anywhere in this book, so calling the unit an oracle ascribes a speech class the witness does not carry. The signal-key finding needs refining rather than upholding as framed: the listed key names the poem's closing PE mark but does not use the barred parashah prefix, so it is not a straight taxonomy violation; the substance holds, in that a tier-3 single-witness mark class travels into the structured signal list under a different prefix without the caveats its disclosure requires, while the row's prose already carries a compliant version - prefix evasion, low on its own. The declared false positives are confirmed genuine: the note at 4:21 attaches to the dwelling participle, ketiv יושבתי against qere יוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת (oshb:Lam.4.21), not to the spliced address, and device_notes discloses the note, so the writer's disposition stands. The span is not contested and the one-apostrophe-or-two question stays held open at low-side confidence with the frontier flag set.
rulings.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: replace 'the shared cup/iniquity vocabulary across both verses' with the ground the bytes carry - the two-token address to Edom standing in both verses - with its digit-bearing sweep (2 verses book-wide, both inside this span). literature_type_guess: drop 'oracle' and keep the address class, an apostrophe to Edom in the poet's own voice, since the substrate carries no divine speech. observed_substrate_signals: remove the key naming the poem-closing mark and leave that disclosure to prose, where the single-witness and weak-corroboration caveats can travel with it. Tests the cure must pass: every cohesion ground must name a term a sweep places in both verses it is said to join, with its object and unit; every genre or speech-class label must be re-derived from the pointed forms; and no structured signal key may name a parashah mark class under any prefix.
